## Setup {.smaller .scrollable}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readxl)
library(ggthemes)
library(paletteer)
library(patchwork)
library(productplots)  # mosaic plots (ggmosaic does not work with ggplot2 4.x yet)

# Load data with all transformations
bp_data <- read_excel("../../data/PublicHealth_BP_Dataset.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(
    SysBP_Change = SysBP_6m - SysBP_0m,
    DiaBP_Change = DiaBP_6m - DiaBP_0m,
    AgeGroup = cut(Age, breaks = c(0, 30, 50, 65, 100),
                   labels = c("18-30", "31-50", "51-65", "65+")),
    Hypertension_Baseline = ifelse(SysBP_0m >= 140 | DiaBP_0m >= 90, 
                                   "Hypertensive", "Normal"),
    BMI_Category = cut(BMI, breaks = c(0, 18.5, 25, 30, 100),
                       labels = c("Underweight", "Normal", "Overweight", "Obese"))
  )

# Time series
bp_time <- bp_data %>%
  select(PatientID, TreatmentGroup, SysBP_0m, SysBP_3m, SysBP_6m) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("SysBP"),
               names_to = "Time", values_to = "SysBP") %>%
  mutate(Months = as.numeric(gsub("SysBP_|m", "", Time)))

# Summary data
bp_summary <- bp_time %>%
  group_by(TreatmentGroup, Months) %>%
  summarise(Mean_SysBP = mean(SysBP, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ci_data <- bp_time %>%
  group_by(TreatmentGroup, Months) %>%
  summarise(Mean = mean(SysBP), SE = sd(SysBP) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

# Custom theme from Module 3
theme_clinical_report <- function(base_size = 12, base_family = "serif") {
  theme_bw(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = base_family),
    plot.title = element_text(size = base_size * 1.3, face = "bold", 
                              hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base_size * 1.1, hjust = 0.5,
                                 color = "gray30", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = base_size * 0.9, hjust = 1,
                                face = "italic", color = "gray50"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = base_size * 1.1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = base_size * 0.9, color = "gray20"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray40", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = base_size, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = base_size * 0.9),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA)
  )
}
```
:::

## Multi-Geom Plot: Points + Line + Ribbon {.smaller .scrollable}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="|6-8|9-11|12-14"}
ggplot(ci_data, 
       aes(x = Months, y = Mean,
           color = TreatmentGroup,
           fill = TreatmentGroup)) +
  # Confidence band
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Mean - 1.96*SE,
                  ymax = Mean + 1.96*SE),
              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  # Trend line
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
  # Data points
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("steelblue", "darkred")) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("steelblue", "darkred"))
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="|4-7|8-9|10-11"}
ggplot(bp_data, 
       aes(x = AgeGroup, y = SysBP_Change,
           fill = TreatmentGroup)) +
  # Individual points with jitter
  geom_jitter(aes(color = TreatmentGroup),
              alpha = 0.3, width = 0.2,
              size = 1.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Box plot overlay
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA) +
  # Add mean as point
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point",
               size = 3, color = "black", shape = 18)
```

## Publication-Ready Plot: All Elements {.smaller .scrollable}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="|1-15|16-23|24-27"}
publication_plot <- ggplot(bp_data, 
                           aes(x = BMI, y = Cholesterol,
                               color = Hypertension_Baseline)) +
  # Data layer
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 1.2) +
  
  # Scales
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Normal" = "forestgreen", "Hypertensive" = "darkred"),
    name = "Baseline BP Status") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(15, 40, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(100, 300, 50)) +
  
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between BMI and Cholesterol",
    subtitle = "Stratified by baseline hypertension status",
    x = "Body Mass Index (kg/m²)",
    y = "Total Cholesterol (mg/dL)",
    caption = "Data: Public Health BP Dataset | n=200 patients | Linear regression with 95% CI"
  ) +
  
  # Theme
  theme_clinical_report(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = c(0.85, 0.15),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black", linewidth = 0.5)
  )
```

# Section 3: Exporting & Reproducibility {background-color="#2C5F8D"}

## ggsave(): Saving Plots {.smaller}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-line-numbers="|1-3|5-10"}
# Create a plot
my_plot <- ggplot(bp_data, aes(x = Age, y = SysBP_0m, color = TreatmentGroup)) +
  geom_point() + theme_minimal()

# Save the plot
ggsave(
  filename = "blood_pressure_analysis.png",
  plot = my_plot,
  width = 10, height = 6, units = "in",
  dpi = 300)
```
:::


::: {.incremental}
- **filename**: File path and name with extension
- **plot**: ggplot object (defaults to last plot displayed)
- **width, height**: Dimensions
- **units**: "in" (inches), "cm", "mm", "px"
- **dpi**: Resolution (72 = screen, 300 = print quality, 600 = high-res print)
:::

## Supported File Formats {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Raster (Pixel-based)**:

- **PNG** - Best for web, presentations
- **JPEG** - Photos, small file size
- **TIFF** - High-quality archival


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggsave("plot.png", dpi = 300)
ggsave("plot.jpg", dpi = 150)
ggsave("plot.tiff", dpi = 600)
```
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Vector (Scalable)**:

- **PDF** - Publications, printing
- **SVG** - Web, editing in Illustrator
- **EPS** - Legacy publications


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggsave("plot.pdf", width = 8, 
       height = 6)
ggsave("plot.svg")
ggsave("plot.eps")
```
:::

:::
::::

## Choosing the Right Format {.smaller}

| Format | Use Case | Pros | Cons |
|--------|----------|------|------|
| **PNG** | Web, presentations, reports | Lossless, transparent background | Large files |
| **PDF** | Publications, printing | Scalable, professional | Requires PDF reader |
| **SVG** | Web, further editing | Scalable, editable | Not all software supports |
| **JPEG** | Web (photos) | Small files | Lossy compression |
| **TIFF** | Archival, high-res | Lossless, high quality | Very large files |

::: {.fragment}
**Recommendation**: Use **PDF** for publications, **PNG** (300 dpi) for presentations/reports
:::

## Reproducibility Best Practices {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Set seed** for random elements (jitter, sampling)

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(123)
```
:::


2. **Document R and package versions**

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sessionInfo()
```
:::


3. **Use relative paths**, not absolute

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Good: read_excel("data/bp_data.xlsx")
# Bad:  read_excel("C:/Users/John/Documents/data/bp_data.xlsx")
```
:::


4. **Version control** with Git/GitHub
5. **Use R Projects** for project organization
:::

# Section 4: Limitations of ggplot2 {background-color="#2C5F8D"}

## What ggplot2 Cannot Do Well {.smaller}

While ggplot2 is powerful, it has limitations:

::: {.incremental}
1. **Mosaic plots / Marimekko charts** - Use `productplots`, `ggmosaic` or base R `mosaicplot()`
2. **3D plots** - Not natively supported, use `plotly` or `rgl`
3. **Network graphs** - Use `ggraph` or `igraph`
4. **Interactive plots** - Limited, need `plotly::ggplotly()` or `ggiraph`
5. **Sankey diagrams** - Use `ggalluvial` or `networkD3`
6. **Circular plots** (beyond polar) - Use `circlize`
7. **Very complex statistical diagrams** - May need specialized packages
:::

## Mosaic Plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
**ggplot2 has no mosaic geom**


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# productplots draws one with ggplot2
library(productplots)

prodplot(bp_data,
         ~ TreatmentGroup + SmokingStatus,
         mosaic()) +
  aes(fill = TreatmentGroup)
```
:::


::: {.fragment}
Or use base R `mosaicplot()` for traditional mosaic plots

## When to Use Alternatives {.smaller .scrollable}

| Need | ggplot2 Solution | Better Alternative |
|------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Mosaic plots | ❌ Not supported | `productplots`, `ggmosaic`, base `mosaicplot()` |
| 3D visualization | ❌ Not supported | `plotly`, `rgl`, `plot3D` |
| Network graphs | ❌ Not supported | `ggraph`, `igraph`, `visNetwork` |
| Interactive plots | Limited | `plotly`, `ggiraph`, `highcharter` |
| Animated plots | Via `gganimate` | `gganimate`, `plotly` |
| Sankey diagrams | ❌ Not supported | `ggalluvial`, `networkD3` |
| Circular plots | Limited (`coord_polar`) | `circlize` |
| Geographic maps | Basic | `leaflet`, `tmap`, `sf` |

## ggplot2 Extensions Ecosystem {.smaller .scrollable}

**The good news**: The ggplot2 ecosystem is vast!

::: {.incremental}
- **productplots** / **ggmosaic** - Mosaic plots
- **gganimate** - Animation
- **ggraph** - Network/tree diagrams
- **ggalluvial** - Sankey/alluvial diagrams
- **ggiraph** - Interactive graphics
- **patchwork** / **cowplot** - Combining plots
- **ggridges** - Ridge line plots
- **ggrepel** - Smart label placement
- **ggforce** - Additional geoms and stats
- **ggsci** - Scientific journal color palettes
:::

::: {.fragment}
**See**: https://exts.ggplot2.tidyverse.org/ for comprehensive list
:::

# Section 5: Best Practices & Common Pitfalls {background-color="#2C5F8D"}

## Common Pitfalls to Avoid {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Mapping constants inside aes()** - Use fixed values outside aes
2. **Too many aesthetics** - Limit to 3-4 visual encodings max
3. **Poor color choices** - Always test for colorblind accessibility
4. **Overplotting** - Use alpha, jitter, or facets
5. **Misleading axes** - Always start at zero for bar charts
6. **Too much clutter** - Remove unnecessary grid lines, legends, or decorations
7. **Inconsistent themes** - Use theme_set() for consistency
8. **Ignoring aspect ratios** - Consider final output dimensions
9. **Not saving properly** - Use appropriate format and resolution
10. **Forgetting reproducibility** - Set seed, document packages
:::

## Best Practices Checklist {.smaller}

Before finalizing visualizations:

::: {.incremental}
- ☐ **Color**: Use colorblind-friendly palettes (viridis, ColorBrewer)
- ☐ **Contrast**: Ensure sufficient contrast between elements
- ☐ **Text size**: Minimum 10pt for body text, 12pt+ for titles
- ☐ **Redundancy**: Don't rely on color alone (use shape, pattern, labels)
- ☐ **Simplicity**: Remove unnecessary elements
- ☐ **Labels**: Clear, descriptive axis labels and titles
- ☐ **Alt text**: Provide text description for screen readers
- ☐ **Print**: Test in grayscale/black & white
- ☐ **Simulation**: Test with colorblind simulator
- ☐ **Font**: Use readable fonts (avoid decorative fonts)
:::

## The ggplot2 Building Process {.smaller}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(data, aes(x = var1, y = var2)) +           # 1. Data + Aesthetics
  geom_point(aes(color = var3, size = var4)) +     # 2. Geometry + Local aes
  scale_color_viridis_d() +                        # 3. Scales
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 6)) +         # 4. More scales
  facet_wrap(~ var5) +                             # 5. Facets
  labs(title = "My Plot",                          # 6. Labels
       x = "X Label", y = "Y Label") +
  theme_minimal() +                                # 7. Theme
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",                # 8. Theme customization
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```
:::


# Section 6: Workshop Summary {background-color="#2C5F8D"}

## Key Takeaways {.smaller}

::: {.incremental}
1. **Grammar of Graphics** provides a systematic framework for building visualizations
2. **Layering** is fundamental - data → aesthetics → geometries → scales → themes
3. **Aesthetics** map data to visual properties (inside `aes()`)
4. **Geoms** are the building blocks - choose appropriately for your data type
5. **Themes** control appearance - use built-in or create custom ones
6. **Colors** matter - always consider colorblind accessibility
7. **Scales** control how data maps to aesthetics - customize breaks, limits, labels
8. **Facets** enable small multiples for comparing groups
9. **Consistency** is key - use global themes and organizational standards
10. Know ggplot2's **limitations** and when to use alternatives
:::

<script>
/* ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
 * quiz.js — tiny self-check quiz engine for reveal.js / any HTML page
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Vanilla JS, zero dependencies, works offline (file://) and inside
 * Quarto reveal.js decks with embed-resources.
 *
 * SYNTAX (what lives in the .qmd — a Pandoc fenced div with data-attrs)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------
 *   MCQ (single answer)
 *   ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="<hash>"
 *         data-show="<base64>" data-explain="<base64>"}
 *   Which model suits a binary outcome?
 *
 *   - Linear regression
 *   - Logistic regression
 *   - Cox regression
 *   :::
 *
 *   Fill-in-the-blank
 *   ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="s1q4" data-type="fill" data-hashes="<h1>,<h2>"
 *         data-show="<base64>" data-explain="<base64>"}
 *   Which gtsummary function builds Table 1?
 *   :::
 *
 *   data-qid      unique id (it salts the hashes)
 *   data-hash     hash of the correct option INDEX (0-based) — mcq
 *   data-hashes   comma-separated hashes of each accepted answer — fill
 *   data-show     base64 of the text revealed by "Show answer"
 *   data-explain  base64 of the short explanation (basic `code` allowed)
 *
 * You never write those attributes by hand. Use the R helpers in
 * assets/quiz.R, which take PLAIN text and emit the fenced div:
 *
 *   ```{r}
 *   #| echo: false
 *   #| output: asis
 *   source("assets/quiz.R")
 *   quiz_mcq("s1q1", "Which model suits a binary outcome?",
 *            c("Linear", "Logistic", "Cox"), answer = 2,
 *            explain = "Binary outcome -> logit link -> logistic.")
 *   quiz_fill("s1q4", "Which gtsummary function builds Table 1?",
 *             accept = c("tbl_summary", "tbl_summary()"),
 *             explain = "tbl_summary() summarises variables, optionally by a group.")
 *   ```
 *
 * Optional: <span class="quiz-score"></span> anywhere shows "x / y", followed by
 *   "Save score" (downloads a text file) and "Reset" buttons. The first-attempt
 *   results are kept in localStorage per deck, so a reload keeps the score.
 *
 * BEHAVIOUR
 *   - MCQ: options are SHUFFLED at load (hash uses the authored index, so
 *     data-hash is unaffected; add data-shuffle="0" to keep authored order).
 *     Click an option -> instant ✔/✘; explanation appears after the
 *     attempt (or after "Show answer").
 *   - Fill: type + Enter / "Check". Answers are normalised (case,
 *     surrounding/duplicate whitespace, backticks, trailing "()") before
 *     hashing, so "  TBL_Summary() " matches "tbl_summary".
 *   - Answers are NOT in the page source: only salted hashes are, and the
 *     explanation / reveal text is base64-encoded. This stops casual
 *     view-source peeking; it is NOT cryptographic security.
 *
 * HASH (must match quiz.R exactly): two polynomial rolling hashes over
 *   the string  qid + "|" + value , base-36 encoded and concatenated.
 * ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var M1 = 2147483629, M2 = 2147483587;

  function hash(str) {
    var a = 5381, b = 52711;
    for (var i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
      var c = str.charCodeAt(i);
      a = (a * 131 + c) % M1;
      b = (b * 137 + c) % M2;
    }
    return a.toString(36) + '.' + b.toString(36);
  }

  function normalise(s) {
    return String(s).toLowerCase()
      .replace(/`/g, '')
      .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
      .trim()
      .replace(/\(\s*\)$/, '')   // "tbl_summary()" == "tbl_summary"
      .trim();
  }

  function b64(s) {
    if (!s) return '';
    try {
      var bin = atob(s), bytes = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
      for (var i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) bytes[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
      return new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(bytes);
    } catch (e) { return ''; }
  }

  function esc(s) {
    return s.replace(/&/g, '&').replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>');
  }
  // escape first, then allow `code` only
  function lite(s) { return esc(s).replace(/`([^`]+)`/g, '<code>$1</code>'); }

  var state = { total: 0, correct: 0, scored: {} };

  // ── saved score ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The first-attempt result of each question is kept in the browser
  // (localStorage, one entry per deck file), so a reload keeps the score.
  // "Save score" downloads a small text file a participant can keep or
  // hand in; "Reset" clears the saved result for this deck.
  var deckName = (location.pathname.split('/').pop() || 'deck').replace(/\.html?$/, '');
  // Kept per workshop folder and deck: deck file names repeat across workshops
  // (s5_choose_check_report is in three). Older versions used the deck name alone; that copy
  // is read once, for this deck's questions only, so no saved score is lost.
  var folder = location.pathname.split('/').slice(-2, -1)[0] || '';
  var STORE = 'quiz-score:' + (folder ? folder + '/' : '') + deckName;
  var LEGACY = 'quiz-score:' + deckName;
  function persist() { try { localStorage.setItem(STORE, JSON.stringify(state.scored)); } catch (e) {} }
  function restore() {
    try {
      var saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORE));
      var migrate = !saved && STORE !== LEGACY;
      if (!saved) saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LEGACY)) || {};
      var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
      for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) {
        var id = qs[i].getAttribute('data-qid');
        if (saved.hasOwnProperty(id)) { state.scored[id] = !!saved[id]; if (saved[id]) state.correct++; }
      }
      if (migrate && Object.keys(state.scored).length) persist();
    } catch (e) {}
  }
  // Reset: forget this deck's answers, also in the old shared copy (other decks keep theirs there).
  function forget() {
    try {
      localStorage.removeItem(STORE);
      var old = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(LEGACY));
      if (old && STORE !== LEGACY) {
        var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
        for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) delete old[qs[i].getAttribute('data-qid')];
        if (Object.keys(old).length) localStorage.setItem(LEGACY, JSON.stringify(old)); else localStorage.removeItem(LEGACY);
      }
    } catch (e) {}
  }
  function scoreText() {
    var lines = ['Quiz score', 'Deck: ' + (document.title || deckName), 'File: ' + deckName, 'Saved: ' + new Date().toLocaleString(),
                 'Score (first attempt): ' + state.correct + ' / ' + state.total, ''];
    var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
    for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) {
      var id = qs[i].getAttribute('data-qid');
      lines.push(id + ': ' + (state.scored.hasOwnProperty(id) ? (state.scored[id] ? 'correct' : 'not correct') : 'not attempted'));
    }
    return lines.join('\n') + '\n';
  }
  function download() {
    var a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = 'data:text/plain;charset=utf-8,' + encodeURIComponent(scoreText());
    a.download = 'quiz_' + deckName + '.txt';
    document.body.appendChild(a); a.click(); a.remove();
  }
  function addScoreTools() {
    var els = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-score');
    for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) {
      if (els[i].getAttribute('data-tools')) continue;
      els[i].setAttribute('data-tools', '1');
      var box = document.createElement('span'); box.className = 'quiz-score-tools';
      var sv = document.createElement('button'); sv.type = 'button'; sv.className = 'quiz-btn quiz-btn-ghost quiz-save'; sv.textContent = 'Save score';
      sv.addEventListener('click', download);
      var rs = document.createElement('button'); rs.type = 'button'; rs.className = 'quiz-btn quiz-btn-ghost quiz-reset'; rs.textContent = 'Reset';
      rs.addEventListener('click', function () { forget(); location.reload(); });
      box.appendChild(sv); box.appendChild(rs);
      els[i].parentNode.insertBefore(box, els[i].nextSibling);
    }
  }

  function updateScores() {
    var els = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-score');
    for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) {
      els[i].textContent = state.correct + ' / ' + state.total;
    }
  }

  function record(qid, ok) {
    if (state.scored.hasOwnProperty(qid)) return;      // first attempt only
    state.scored[qid] = !!ok;
    if (ok) state.correct++;

    updateScores();
  }

  function feedback(q, ok, msg) {
    var fb = q.querySelector('.quiz-feedback');
    fb.className = 'quiz-feedback ' + (ok ? 'is-correct' : 'is-wrong');
    fb.innerHTML = (ok ? '✔ Correct. ' : '✘ Not quite. ') + (msg ? lite(msg) : '');
  }

  function explanation(q) {
    var ex = b64(q.getAttribute('data-explain'));
    return ex;
  }

  function buildCommon(q) {
    var fb = document.createElement('div');
    fb.className = 'quiz-feedback';
    fb.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
    q.appendChild(fb);

    var show = document.createElement('button');
    show.type = 'button';
    show.className = 'quiz-btn quiz-btn-ghost';
    show.textContent = 'Show answer';
    q.appendChild(show);
    return { fb: fb, show: show };
  }

  function initMCQ(q) {
    var qid = q.getAttribute('data-qid');
    var correctHash = q.getAttribute('data-hash');
    var list = q.querySelector('ul, ol');
    if (!list) return;
    // authored index is what the hash is built on; DISPLAY order is shuffled so the
    // answer position (and any length/position tell) cannot be learned.
    var items = Array.prototype.slice.call(list.children).map(function (li, i) { return { li: li, i: i }; });
    if (q.getAttribute('data-shuffle') !== '0') {
      for (var k = items.length - 1; k > 0; k--) {
        var r = Math.floor(Math.random() * (k + 1)), t = items[k]; items[k] = items[r]; items[r] = t;
      }
    }
    var wrap = document.createElement('div');
    wrap.className = 'quiz-options';
    var btns = items.map(function (it, pos) {
      var b = document.createElement('button');
      b.type = 'button';
      b.className = 'quiz-option';
      b.setAttribute('data-i', it.i);
      b.innerHTML = '<span class="quiz-letter">' + String.fromCharCode(65 + pos) + '</span>' + it.li.innerHTML;
      wrap.appendChild(b);
      return b;
    });
    list.parentNode.replaceChild(wrap, list);
    var c = buildCommon(q);

    function isCorrect(i) { return hash(qid + '|' + i) === correctHash; }
    function orig(b) { return parseInt(b.getAttribute('data-i'), 10); }
    function reveal() {
      btns.forEach(function (b) { if (isCorrect(orig(b))) b.classList.add('is-correct'); });
    }

    btns.forEach(function (b) {
      b.addEventListener('click', function () {
        var ok = isCorrect(orig(b));
        b.classList.add(ok ? 'is-correct' : 'is-wrong');
        record(qid, ok);
        feedback(q, ok, explanation(q));
        if (ok) btns.forEach(function (x) { x.disabled = true; });
      });
    });
    c.show.addEventListener('click', function () {
      reveal();
      record(qid, false);
      var ans = b64(q.getAttribute('data-show'));
      var fb = q.querySelector('.quiz-feedback');
      fb.className = 'quiz-feedback is-info';
      fb.innerHTML = 'Answer: <strong>' + lite(ans) + '</strong>. ' + lite(explanation(q));
      btns.forEach(function (x) { x.disabled = true; });
    });
  }

  function initFill(q) {
    var qid = q.getAttribute('data-qid');
    var accepted = (q.getAttribute('data-hashes') || '').split(',');
    var row = document.createElement('div');
    row.className = 'quiz-fill';
    var input = document.createElement('input');
    input.type = 'text';
    input.className = 'quiz-input';
    input.placeholder = 'type your answer…';
    input.setAttribute('autocomplete', 'off');
    input.setAttribute('autocapitalize', 'off');
    input.setAttribute('spellcheck', 'false');
    var check = document.createElement('button');
    check.type = 'button';
    check.className = 'quiz-btn';
    check.textContent = 'Check';
    row.appendChild(input);
    row.appendChild(check);
    q.appendChild(row);
    var c = buildCommon(q);

    function submit() {
      var v = normalise(input.value);
      if (!v) return;
      var ok = accepted.indexOf(hash(qid + '|' + v)) !== -1;
      input.classList.remove('is-correct', 'is-wrong');
      input.classList.add(ok ? 'is-correct' : 'is-wrong');
      record(qid, ok);
      feedback(q, ok, explanation(q));

    check.addEventListener('click', submit);
    // keep reveal.js shortcuts (space, arrows, f, s, …) out of the text box
    ['keydown', 'keyup', 'keypress'].forEach(function (ev) {
      input.addEventListener(ev, function (e) {
        e.stopPropagation();
        if (ev === 'keydown' && e.key === 'Enter') submit();
      });
    });
    c.show.addEventListener('click', function () {
      record(qid, false);
      var fb = q.querySelector('.quiz-feedback');
      fb.className = 'quiz-feedback is-info';
      fb.innerHTML = 'Answer: <strong>' + lite(b64(q.getAttribute('data-show'))) + '</strong>. ' + lite(explanation(q));
    });

  function init() {
    var qs = document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-q');
    state.total = qs.length;
    for (var i = 0; i < qs.length; i++) {
      var q = qs[i];
      if (q.getAttribute('data-quiz-ready')) continue;
      q.setAttribute('data-quiz-ready', '1');
      var type = q.getAttribute('data-type');
      if (type === 'mcq') initMCQ(q);
      else if (type === 'fill') initFill(q);

    addScoreTools();
    updateScores();

## Bonus: Combining Plots with patchwork {.smaller .scrollable}


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(patchwork)

# Create individual plots
p1 <- ggplot(bp_data, aes(x = Age, y = SysBP_0m)) + geom_point()
p2 <- ggplot(bp_data, aes(x = BMI, y = Cholesterol)) + geom_point()
p3 <- ggplot(bp_data, aes(x = Region, y = SysBP_0m)) + geom_boxplot()
p4 <- ggplot(bp_data, aes(x = SysBP_Change)) + geom_histogram()

# Combine in various layouts
p1 + p2 + p3 + p4                    # Side by side
(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)                # Grid
p1 / (p2 | p3)                       # Complex layout
```
:::


::: {.fragment}
**patchwork** makes combining plots intuitive with `+`, `|`, and `/` operators

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
